subject: OrchardFlow pilot: plan composition and safe rollback path
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@orchardflow.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot packaging — capacity vs feature trade for OrchardFlow

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. OrchardFlow is ready to run a 6‑week pilot but we need help deciding the right composition: do we lean throughput-first (higher token capacity, narrower feature set) or feature-first (full feature bundle at lower throughput)? Our internal stakeholders care about:

- Latency for real-time scoring (must be <250ms p95)
- Cost predictability for budgeting the pilot
- A clear downgrade/rollback path if usage spikes or quality issues appear

Can you sketch two concrete pilot options with: baseline throughput, included features, upgrade trigger, and a rollback / canary plan? Also copy in procurement so we can fast-track the paperwork.

Procurement contact: procurement@orchardflow.com

Appreciate a short one-pager and rough pricing.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of Product, OrchardFlow

[external attachment: product-reqs-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@orchardflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging — capacity vs feature trade for OrchardFlow

Marta — thanks for the clear brief. High level: we recommend two defensible pilot compositions and an explicit canary/rollback policy so procurement can sign quickly. Attached is a 1-page comparison plus a master amendment draft.

Option A (Throughput-first pilot)
- Focus: sustained token throughput, narrower feature set (inference + basic chat + embeddings)
- Provisioning: reserved 2x GPU pool sized for 500k tokens/day average, burst to 1.2M tokens/day for 1 hour windows
- SLA target: p95 latency <250ms for short prompts; we target <200ms typical
- Upgrade trigger: sustained daily usage >700k tokens for 5 consecutive days OR customer request after QA pass
- Rollback: automatic fallback to compact model variant + temporary throttling policy; canary on 10% of traffic for 24h before full rollout

Option B (Feature-first pilot)
- Focus: full feature set (tools + structured output) at smaller baseline throughput
- Provisioning: reserved 1x GPU pool, burst enabled to 400k tokens/day
- SLA target: p95 latency <350ms for rich-tool invocations
- Upgrade trigger: feature acceptance on our eval set + usage >250k tokens/day for 7 days
- Rollback: disable heavy-tool paths and migrate to simple prompt flow; canary for feature toggles at 5% traffic for 48h

Commercial note (high level)
- Pilot length: 6 weeks preferred. We usually propose a pilot credit that converts into an uplift if OrchardFlow converts to committed capacity.
- Attached: Orchard_Pilot_Proposal_v1.pdf and MA_Draft_Orchard.docx for procurement review.

Next steps
1) Tell us which option you want to run — we can turn around SOW + DocuSign in 24 business hours.
2) Share your expected weekly traffic profile so we can validate pool sizing.
3) If you want, I can loop in Karthik for quantization/throughput advice.

Onward —
Aditya Rao
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Thanks Aditya — good split. A few commercial guardrails from our side:

- Pilot discount: we typically offer a pilot credit equal to 15% of estimated pilot spend (applied up-front as invoice credit). That helps shorten procurement cycles.
- Conversion credit: if OrchardFlow converts to a 12‑month committed Dedicated plan within 90 days of pilot end, we credit 25% of pilot spend against first invoice.
- Downgrade clarity: we will include a one-time rollback fee cap for abrupt de-provisioning (to protect reserved capacity).
- Add-on recommendation: enable burst autoscaling add-on during the pilot to avoid missed SLA windows; we can price that as metered for the pilot and convert to reserved on commit.

Numbers-wise — assuming Option A sizing above and our standard pilot rates, the pilot spend estimate is ~USD 28k–35k (depending on burst hours). If Marta confirms Option A, I’ll draft a short commercial term sheet and a redline to the MA draft.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

P.S. Aditya — happy to take the conversion math offline; Karthik can chime in on quantization choices that might lower the spend band by ~10–15%.
